comments.value: I would like to explain once again what communication will look like when using a voice translator. For example, I speak English, and there are three people next to me who speak English, Spanish and Japanese. Each of my conversation partners has his native language in the game settings: ENG, SPA, JPN, respectively. I have a good microphone, so I turn on the translator mode with the option of «Quick Translation». In «Quick Translation» mode you can see the text you have entered, but you cannot edit it. In order to say something, you must press and hold the «SPEAK» button. My conversation partner, who, like me, speaks English, hears my speech immediately. He hears my real voice. He doesn't need a translation. All other people don’t hear my voice and they see an special icon above my avatar that indicates that speech-to-text is being converted. As soon as I finish speaking, I release the «SPEAK» button and the text in my native language is transmitted to my Spanish and Japanese speaking interlocutors. They can't see the text itself. The text message is transmitted through the game's internal mechanisms. The received message is translated on their client side, in accordance with their language settings, and pronounced through a speech synthesizer. The transmission of such data packets is limited by the distance to the interlocutor. That is, people standing very far from me will not receive such messages. Also, the volume of the speech synthesizer depends on the distance to the interlocutor. If an error occurs during the dictation, you can delete the text you have entered with the second «RESET» button. If a person has a bad microphone and the quality of speech recognition is low, he should disable the «Quick Translation» mode. In this case he will be able to edit the text and confirm sending the message.

details: I propose to introduce two modes of voice communication: 1) direct communication; 2) communication through an electronic translator with voice recognition system and speech synthesis. Direct communication mode is used in VRChat now and here comments are unnecessary. Let us consider the 2nd mode in more detail. Each user in his game settings indicates his native language. If the user activates the 2nd mode, but his conversation partner has the same native language, then the "1st mode, direct communication mode" still works. However, if the native languages of the interlocutor are different, then at first all spoken words are converted into text, which can be edited if you want. Then, when you press the "TRANSLATION" button, the text is translated and spoken using a speech synthesizer for each interlocutor according to their language settings. That is, if there are several interlocutors, each of them will hear the speech in his own language, and they will not hear my real voice. Translated text, if desired, can be displayed for only one language that we choose. This will allow people who know the language to appreciate the quality of the translation. Thus, if the 2nd communication mode is enabled, my original voice will only be heard by people who have the same native language as mine. Everyone else will be able to hear the speech synthesizer. If I am sure of the reliability of speech recognition and the quality of translation, you can activate the fast translation mode in the settings. In this mode, I press and hold the talk button. During this time, speech is converted to text. As soon as I release the button, the text is immediately translated into other languages without any checks and is pronounced. If you look at the mechanism of interaction in more detail, the following happens. When I say something, the only thing that happens on my game client is to convert speech into text. Then this text is transferred to the game clients of my interlocutors, and there the text is translated into the appropriate language and converted into speech. In addition, you can add voice filters that change the timbre of the speech synthesizer voice. Then, in addition to the text, my voice settings will also be transmitted to my conversation partners. There are various free translation services. For example, Google Translate, Microsoft Translate, DeepL, etc. In the VRChat game, you just need to create the appropriate interface to use them. I want the game to remove the language barrier and so that people from different cultures can communicate with each other.
title: Using an electronic translator and speech synthesizer for communication
